_comment: Craft of the Bobiverse: Heaven design generations, named hulls, colony and Exodus ships, Medeiros/Brazilian probe line, Others death asteroids and cargo fleet. Design generation is not the same thing as a hull name. Holotank plates hang on vessels/<id>. Bob records keep a free-text vessel field; when it matches `match` here, the dossier links into this register.

vessels.name: Heaven design, generation 1
vessels.note: The first HEAVEN is a converted interplanetary freighter: body split for a midships SURGE ring, reactor in place of the fusion stack, viewports shut. Elliptical cross-section, airlocks and cargo doors everywhere, running lights red and green plus blue for three-axis travel. The chapter says it is not a pretty ship — no flagship lines, no shuttle aerodynamics. This is the design step, not every hull later named Heaven-something.

vessels.name: Heaven design, generation 2
vessels.note: Version-2 HEAVEN: larger frame, bigger SURGE and reactor, more replicant and storage volume, a rail-gun, and buster stowage and launch. One of the new hulls is a trade-up for the original. Hull names like Heaven-2 or Heaven-3 are individual ships, not this generation number.

vessels.name: Heaven design, combat class
vessels.note: Combat-class HEAVEN (Heaven-9 and Heaven-10 among them): roughly ten g, oversized SURGE and main reactor, a second small well-shielded reactor for dark coasting, doubled busters, rail-guns on the big drive, and SUDDAR jamming. Freighter DNA made mean rather than a clean navy destroyer.

vessels.name: Heaven design, carbon-black
vessels.note: Not a new silhouette: the combat line painted into near invisibility. Carbon-black exterior, almost zero albedo, radar-quiet military profiles, heavier shielding, radio silence — vulnerable mainly on SUDDAR. Cool factor is paint and quiet systems, not a redesign.

vessels.name: HEAVEN-1B
vessels.note: The original's own hull after the first conversion — the ship that is him in the early chapters. Design generation 1; the plate for that design lives on the design entry.

vessels.name: Heaven-2
vessels.note: Riker's hull. The name is a hull serial, not 'design generation 2' — the generation number and the ship name are different systems in the books and here.

vessels.name: Heaven-3
vessels.note: Bill's early hull at Epsilon Eridani. Same design era as the version-2 line.

vessels.name: Heaven-6
vessels.note: Homer's hull. On the register as the ship he is associated with in the first volume and after; fate of the vessel and fate of the Bob are graded separately.

vessels.name: Heaven-8
vessels.note: Linus's hull — he identifies it by name when he hails the Australian probe at Epsilon Indi. Same version-3 cohort as Calvin and Goku; the oversized combat specs in that design pass are called out for Heaven-9 and Heaven-10, not for this ship.

vessels.name: Heaven-9
vessels.note: Combat-class hull assigned to Calvin for the Alpha Centauri run. Specced with Heaven-10 in the same design pass.

vessels.name: Heaven-10
vessels.note: Combat-class hull assigned to Goku. Pair to Heaven-9 in Bill's beefed-up ship specs.

vessels.name: Version-5 HEAVEN
vessels.note: The version-5 HEAVEN class as the later books label it — Neil and Herschel among those flying it. Exterior text for generation 5 is thinner than for 1–4; this entry holds the class name until more design detail is worth its own plate.

vessels.name: Colony ship
vessels.note: The colony transports that carried settlers and their Bobs. Three records on file name this class rather than a unique hull number: Owen, Jack and Isaac. Not a Heaven; a different job.

vessels.name: Exodus-1
vessels.note: Bert's Exodus hull as listed in the printed genealogy. Exodus ships are the large human-transport line, not HEAVEN war hulls.

vessels.name: Exodus-2
vessels.note: Ernie's Exodus hull in the printed genealogy.

vessels.name: Exodus-3
vessels.note: Sam bringing Exodus-3 in — colony transport work at the Vulcan/Romulus end of the story.

vessels.name: Exodus-7
vessels.note: Dexter's Exodus hull as the Cast of Characters lists him. Same line as the other Exodus transports.

vessels.name: Serra do Mar
vessels.note: Brazilian Empire ship that answers Bob at Epsilon Eridani: Major Ernesto Medeiros on the audio link. The first named enemy hull in the series, and the template the later Brazilian probes are compared to. Not a Heaven — FAITH's rival programme, same interstellar race.

vessels.name: Medeiros probe (Brazilian)
vessels.note: Brazilian probes similar to the Serra do Mar, almost certainly run by Medeiros clones. Riker meets them in Sol with decoy work and busters; the same family of craft keeps turning up wherever a Brazilian seed got through. Class entry rather than one hull — the books treat them as a threat type.

vessels.name: Death asteroid
vessels.note: The Others' world-killing platforms. Bill's first good look at a convoy counts ten of them among attendants and cargo hulks; later engagements scale that count up. They rotate to bring transmitter grids to bear and are what strip a biosphere before the scavenger fleet moves in. Weapon-class craft rather than a ship you board — filed here because the books name them as hardware in the fleet, not as weather.

vessels.name: Others cargo vessel
vessels.note: Huge cylindrical hulks in the Others' convoy — on the order of ten kilometres long and a kilometre across, more planetoid than ship. Cargo carriers for ants and fighters; Herschel later drifts between two of them outside Delta Pavonis. Not death asteroids: different job, same empire.

vessels.name: Others attendant
vessels.note: Small AMI-controlled craft that travel with the Others' capital units — Bill puts them as roughly equivalent to busters, present by the hundred. Escorts and defenders rather than planet-killers; the swarm around the death asteroids and cargo ships.
